claims.text: Deliberately NOT a ``ValueError``: every other refusal in :func:`convene` is a malformed-roster complaint, and "you were about to spend money" must be catchable on its own.
claims.why: The claim refers to other refusals in convene, which are not present in this chunk.

claims.text: Name every seat that could actually reach a vendor.  FAIL-CLOSED.
claims.why: The function implements fail-closed by defaulting to live unless certain conditions are met.

claims.text: it is not one of the shipped concrete adapters at all (the base ``CouncilAdapter._dispatch`` raises ``NotImplementedError``, so a class defined elsewhere is the caller's own code and the caller owns it);
claims.why: The check uses shipped_classes tuple built from _vendors module; the behavior of _dispatch is not verified in this chunk.

claims.text: its ``_dispatch`` -- the transport seam -- is defined OUTSIDE :mod:`daedalus.council.vendors`, i.e. the test/host replaced it;
its ``runner`` / ``chat`` hook is not one of :data:`_SHIPPED_TRANSPORTS`, i.e. a substitute was injected at construction.
claims.why: _SHIPPED_TRANSPORTS is not defined in this chunk; the function checks hooks against it but its value is unknown.

claims.text: If :data:`_SHIPPED_TRANSPORTS` ever resolves empty (vendors renamed something), the hook test is SKIPPED rather than trivially satisfied, so the failure lands on the safe side.
claims.why: Code shows: if _SHIPPED_TRANSPORTS: ... else: skip (substituted remains False).

claims.text: Every one of them is REQUESTED, and every requested participant produces exactly one chained turn per round even when it is missing: skipping an unavailable vendor would let a two-vendor council render identically to a four-vendor one.
claims.why: The claim describes behavior not implemented in this chunk; requires seeing the chaining logic.

claims.text: ``trusted_vendors`` is the OPERATOR OPT-IN that lifts a vendor off the untrusted allow-list for this council only.  It is recorded per participant, because deciding OpenAI or Google is trusted with this repo's IP is a policy decision and a default argument must not make it.
claims.why: The usage of trusted_vendors is not present in this chunk.

claims.text: ``live`` is the SPEND OPT-IN and defaults to False.  Any seat that still carries a shipped vendor transport (:func:`live_egress_seats`) raises :class:`LiveCouncilRefused` here -- before the council id, before the store, before the roster is chained, before one byte is dispatched.  Offline adapters (fakes, injected runners) are unaffected, so the replay harness never has to ask for permission it does not need.
claims.why: The live-wire gate logic is not fully present in this chunk; the code after the comment is cut off.

claims.text: Materialised ONCE, before anything inspects it: the live-wire gate below iterates the roster, and a one-shot iterator would arrive here full, be drained by the gate, and reach `sorted()` empty -- a council of nobody, chained as if it were real.
claims.why: The code does participants = tuple(participants) to materialize the sequence.

claims.text: a council with no participants is not a council
claims.why: The code raises ValueError if not participants.
